p.seg: In Guǎngzhōu there is a large tree that can ward off volcanic fires. In the north, it is called "Shènhuǒ" (慎火, "Caution Fire") or "Jièhuǒ" (戒火, "Guard Against Fire").
Many plant it on rooftops to prevent fires.
*Nányuè Zhì* (南越志, Records of Southern Yue)
Southeast of Dōngwǔ (東武) city, there is a "Shènghuǒ Mù" (勝火木, Fire-Conquering Wood), which in the local dialect is called "Tǐngzi" (挺子).
If this wood is burned in a field fire, it will char but not be reduced to ashes. Therefore, Dōngfāng Shuò (東方朔) called it "Bù Huī zhī Mù" (不灰之木, Wood that Does Not Turn to Ash).
Fú Chēn's (伏琛) *Qí Dì Jì* (齊地記, Records of the Land of Qi)
On Xúwú Mountain (徐無山) there are wood that does not turn to ash, and stones that create fire. The commentary says: This wood is black in color, resembling
charcoal, and has no leaves. The stone is red like cinnabar. Rubbing two stones together produces fire.
One could have fire for life, but now there is none.
*Shuǐ Jīng* (水經, The Water Classic)
On the hill of Xiāoqiū (蕭丘) in the South Sea grows a kind of wood, which,
though touched by fire, only becomes slightly charred. People sometimes use it as firewood, and after cooking, extinguish it by dousing it with water.
Its use is inexhaustible.
*Bàopǔ* (抱朴, Master Who Embraces Simplicity)
The "Sīwéi Shù" (思惟樹, Contemplation Tree). During the Hàn (漢) dynasty, a Daoist priest brought many seeds from the Western Regions and planted them at the foot of the west peak of Mount Sōng (嵩).
Later, it grew extremely tall, with four trees that blossomed three times a year.
*Wèi Wáng Huā Mù Zhì* (魏王花木志, Records of Flowers and Trees of the King of Wei)
At Sōnggāo Temple (嵩高寺)
there is a Sīwéi Tree, which is the same as the "bèiduō" (貝多, palm-leaf tree). The Tathāgata sat under the bèiduō to contemplate, hence the name.
*Sōngshān Jì* (嵩山記, Records of Mount Song)
Not far north of Jiànnàbǔluó (建那補羅) kingdom in South India, there is a grove of Talipot palm trees (Duōluó Shù 多羅樹) for more than thirty *lǐ* (里).
Its leaves are long and wide, and its color is bright and lustrous. All countries use them for writing.
*Fānyì* (翻譯, Translation)
The Yìjīn (翊津)
Bridge in Luòyáng (洛陽) leads to the east street of the translation grounds. In the translation grounds are more than ten Brahman monks and monks from India [Shēndú (身毒)].
The scriptures newly translated there come from foreign countries, written on palm-leafs (Bèiduō shù yè 貝多樹葉).
Written in what is now the script of the barbarians. The bèiduō leaves are one *chǐ* (尺) and five or six *cùn* (寸) long, and about five *cùn* wide. The shape of the leaves resembles
a pipa, but is thick and large. They are written horizontally in lines, and according to the amount of scripture, one side is sewn together neatly.
*Shíyí* (拾遺, Supplement)
In Dìng'ān (定安) County in Jiāozhǐ (交趾), there is "Mù Mián" (木緜, tree cotton). The tree is tall, and the pods are the size of wine cups, containing cotton like
wadding. The cotton can also be made into cloth, called "xiè" (緤), also known as "Máobù" (毛布, wool cloth).
*Wú Lù Dìlǐ Zhì* (吳錄地理志, Geographical Records of the State of Wu)
Fifth Title for Heaven
The *Shàngshū Shuō* says:
Heaven has five titles:
When it is revered and lords over (all),
then it is called Huángtiān (皇天);
when the primordial *qì* is vast and great,
then it is called Hàotiān (昊天);
when it benevolently covers and pities those below,
then it is called Mǐntiān (旻天);
when it oversees those below from Heaven,
Then it is called *Shàngtiān* (上天, Supreme Heaven);
viewed from afar,
it appears dark blue,
then it is called *Cāngtiān* (蒼天, Azure Heaven).
The *Zhōu Lǐ Shū* (周禮疏, Subcommentary on the Rites of Zhou)
discusses four names.
The *Ěryǎ* (爾雅, приближающий к классическому) says:
Spring is called *Cāngtiān*,
summer is called *Hàotiān* (昊天, Bright Heaven),
autumn is called *Míntān* (旻天, Autumn Heaven),
winter is called *Shàngtiān*.
Lǐ Xún (李巡) comments:
In spring, all things begin to grow,
and their color is dark blue,
therefore it is called *Cāngtiān*;
in summer, all things are strong and flourishing,
and their breath is vast and bright,
therefore it is called *Hàotiān*;
in autumn, all things mature,
and all have patterns and order,
therefore it is called *Míntān*.
*Mín* (旻) means
pattern and order.
In winter, the *yīn* (陰) *qì* (氣) is above,
and all things lie dormant and hidden,
therefore it is called *Shàngtiān*.
The virtue of the Supreme Purity
Tàiqīng
reaches above to the Great Purity,
and below to the Great Tranquility,
and in the middle to the myriad spirits.
Then auspicious stars shine brightly,
sweet dew descends,
crimson grass grows,
and sweet springs emerge.
*Hé Guānzi*:
The origin of man
Heaven is
the origin of man;
parents are
the root of man.
When man is in dire straits, he returns to his root;
therefore, when weary from toil and exhaustion, one never fails to call upon Heaven,
and in pain and sorrow, one never fails to call upon one's parents.
. *Biography of Qū Yuán* from the *Records of the Grand Historian*
The essence of all yang
Heaven,
the essence of all yang,
combine to form the Grand One,
and are divided into different names.
*Spring and Autumn Sayings and Commentaries*:
The ancestor of all things
Heaven and earth
are where the primordial *qì* originates,
the ancestor of all things.
In the *Lǐ Tǒng* (禮統)
, Dǒng Zhòngshū (董仲舒) said:
"Heaven
is the ancestor of all things.
Therefore, it universally covers and embraces without discrimination,
establishes the sun, moon, wind, and rain to harmonize them,
and regulates *yīn* and *yáng*, cold and heat, to complete them."
*Běn Zhuàn* (本傳):
"The Dà Gāo (大高) sacrifice:
in offering sacrifices to Dà Gāo, the pig is the supreme sacrificial animal."
*Huáinánzǐ Fàn Lùn Xià* (淮南子汜論下):
"Manifest affairs to Shàng Gāo (上高)."
*Chén Shū Shìzǔ Zhào* (陳書世祖詔):
"The essence of all gods—
heaven
is the essence of all gods,
with the sun, moon, and stars as its conspicuous positions."
Zhèng Xuán's (鄭玄) commentary on the *Zhōu Lǐ* (周禮)
*Qīngmíng* (青冥):
In the *Chǔ Cí* (楚辭):
"Grasping *qīngmíng*, I unfurl the rainbow."
Commentary:
Qingming,
means Heaven.
It means the green clouds are distant and obscure.
Tai Yuan
Only Tai Yuan is revered,
and the old woman goddess is Fan Li.
Note:
Tai Yuan,
means Heaven.
The old woman goddess,
means Earth.
"Book of Han"
Shang Xuan
Praying for blessings to Shang Xuan,
thinking about what constitutes reverence.
Pingzi's "Rhapsody on the Eastern Capital"
Tai Hao
Láng Yǐ, in a memorial to the emperor, said:
"Remove disasters and manifest blessings,
obey Heaven and achieve harmony,
reject and expel cruelty and harm,
in order to pacify the common people,
then Tai Hao will be pleased and harmonious,
and the sound of thunder will then be unleashed."
Note:
Tai Hao,
Heaven.
*Hòu Hàn Běn Zhuàn*
*Líng Yào*
Cài Bójie’s "Inscription for Chén Tàiqiū" states:
"He received the essence of mountains and rivers,
and embraced the purity of *líng yào*."
The commentary explains:
"*Líng Yào*
refers to Heaven."
There is an examination in the *Shàngshū Wěi*.
*Líng Yào*,
according to Zhāng Héng's "Ling Xian Huntian Yi", says:
"The root of covering and carrying [i.e., Heaven and Earth],
nothing precedes primordial Qi;
the origin of *líng yào*,
divides Qi to form primordial images."
The multitude of spirits governs
Heaven,
the multitude of spirits is the ruler;
morality, virtue, benevolence, and righteousness
are the Way of Heaven;
trembling with fear
is the heart of Heaven.
Abandoning the Way and destroying virtue
is to despise the Way of Heaven;
being dangerous and narrow, unrestrained and arrogant
Contrary to people's intentions.
. *Lùnhéng Biàn Chóng*
All creatures greatly look up to
Heaven,
which is revolving,
and uniform,
an accumulation of *yang* and pure strength,
its form is revolving,
which all creatures greatly look up to.
It also says:
That which establishes Heaven and Earth
is water;
that which completes Heaven and Earth
is *qi*.
The *qi* of water and earth rises and becomes Heaven.
Yáng Quán's *Wùlǐ Lùn*
The Great Circle
*Wénxuǎn*, Shù Xī's *Bǔ Wáng Shī* says:
How vast and encompassing is the Great Circle,
and boundless are the nine regions of earth.
Lǚ Xiàng commented, saying:
"The Great Circle,
is Heaven."
Note:
The "Lǚshì Chūnqiū" says:
"The Great Circle is above,
and the Great Square is below."
The "Guǎnzi" says:
"If a man can be still and upright,
then he can wear the Great Circle and tread upon the Great Square."
Supreme Divinity.
In the "Wénxuǎn", Yán Yánnián's "Preface to the Crooked Stream Poetry" says:
"To ponder on facing the heart of the Supreme Divinity,
in order to bestow grace on the multitudes of sprouts."
Liú Liáng commented, saying:
"The Supreme Divinity,
is Heaven."
Note:
Cáo Zǐjiàn's "Lament for Emperor Wén of Wei" says:
"The Supreme Divinity sent down auspicious signs,
during the Huángchū era, there was abundant blessing."
In the "History of the Song Dynasty", Jìn Fù Xuán's "Song of Suburban Sacrifice" says:
"I will, day and night,
reverently serve the Supreme Divinity."
In the "Book of Southern Qi", Sòng Xiè Zhuāng's "Words of Ascent Song" says:
"To manifest and serve the former sages,
embracing and cherishing the Supreme Divinity."
It also says:
"To inaugurate the meditation and match the sacrifices,
to truly face the Supreme Divinity."
"Decree of the Empress Dowager Deposing the Prince of Hǎilíng":
"The Supreme Divinity, therefore, carefully attends to the mandate,"
the myriad people therefore return and embrace."
*Liáng Shū*, Emperor Wǔ's "Edict of Abdication":
"I deeply revere the spirits above, and therefore receive this great undertaking."
*Wèi Shū, Péngchéng Wáng Xié Zhuàn*:
"The spirits above have no mirror,
and the sacred body is unwell."
Yuán Zǐgōng's memorial states:
"Suburban sacrifices to Heaven and offerings to the Emperor
are to correspond with the spirits above."
Gāo Lǘ's "Ode to Supreme Virtue" says:
"The spirits above send down their inspection,
and the sagacious Emperor has returned to the right way.
He favors the house of Wèi,
matching Heaven and receiving the mandate."
Jǔqú Méngxùn's memorial states:
"The spirits above send down their blessings,
and destiny returns to the virtuous."
*Líng Zhēng Zhì*, a memorial from the assembled officials:
"The spirits above bestow their regard,
and auspicious omens gather completely."
*Běi Qí Shū*, Gāo Yáng's "Edict of Abdication":
"The spirits above are weary of virtue,
and grant the great mandate to return."
*Běi Shǐ, Wáng Shào Zhuàn, Dì Tōng Jì*:
"Yè Líng Huáng means
that the virtue of the Great Suí accords with the spirits above."
*Suí Shū, Yuè Zhì*:
"The spirits above bestow a hundred blessings,
and all the gods return to a myriad years."
Yuán Yí
. In the "Song Calendar Treatise," Zǔ Chōngzhī's memorial states:
"The first line of the yang trigram
, signifies the beginning of the qi from due north.
The seven constellations of the Black Tortoise
correspond to the position of Zi (the first of the Earthly Branches).
If the round instrument distinguishes directions
, it should be based on the sun.
The location of the winter solstice
ought to be in Xuánxiāo (one of the twelve divisions of the zodiac),
but the current South Pole
is actually located in the eastern corner."
Yuán Líng
Xiè Zhuāng's "Ode to the Moon" says:
"The gentle earth congeals with snow,
The round heaven is like a water mirror."
Lǐ Shàn says:
"The gentle earth
refers to the earth,
the round heaven
refers to the sky."
Yuán Jīng
Yán Yánnián's "Lament for Empress Wényuán" says:
"The round essence first shone,
the square earth began to congeal."
Jì said:
"Yuán jīng,"
refers to Heaven.
The *Jiù Táng Shū* (Old Book of Tang), in Guō Zǐyí's memorial (*Sùzōng Wú Huánghòu Fùmiao Biǎo*) to Emperor Suzong regarding the enshrining of Empress Wu in the ancestral temple, states:
"Yuán jīng" (round essence) embodies quality,
while "fāng zhī" (square reverence) receives grace.
Cānglíng
in Sēng Yán's *Dá Liú Shànmíng* (Reply to Liu Shanming) states:
"In the year of old age,"
"commanding and accomplishing tasks,"
"this is naturally conferred by Cānglíng, using (him) as a tool to achieve success."
The *Hóngmíng Jí* (Collection for the Propagation of Enlightenment),
in Emperor Wu of Zhou's edict (*Zhū Yǔwénhù Zhuīzūn Xiàomǐn Zhào*) executing Yuwen Hu and posthumously honoring Emperor Xiaomin, says:
"(It) accords above with the blessings of Cānglíng,"
"and manifests below the bestowals of Hòu Zhī."
*Zhōu Shū* (Book of Zhou)
Xuán Yí
The *Běi Qí Shū* (Book of Northern Qi) imperial edict says:
"It corresponds above with Xuán Yí,"
"and accords below with rivers and mountains."
Ruler of the Hundred Spirits
Emperor Xuanzong had not yet performed the sacrificial rites in person.
Zhāng Jiǔlíng submitted a memorial saying:
"Heaven,"
"is the ruler of the hundred spirits,"
"and the source from which the king receives his mandate."
Since ancient times, the rulers who inherit the throne
must perform the ritual of suburban sacrifice,
to revere the Mandate of Heaven and repay what they have received.
The *Jiù Táng Shū*
Lí Gàn, the first ancestor of the people,
in "Debate on Suburban Sacrifice," said:
"Heaven is the beginning of all things;
Ancestors are the beginning of man."
The *Xīn Táng Shū*'s original biography, "Treatise on Old Ritual and Ceremony,"
"Earth is the canopy of stars,"
Wáng Biāo in his "Rhapsody on Natural Endowment" says:
"It broadly forms the canopy of the earth,
Vastly creates the hub of stars."
*Qīng Yì Lù*
"Hào Qióng"
Sīmǎ Xiàngrú in his "Letter on the Feng and Shan Sacrifices":
"At the very beginning of ancient times,
Hào Qióng brought forth the people."
Shīgǔ says:
"Hào Qióng,
both refer to Heaven.
Hào refers to the vaporous vastness,
Qióng refers to its dome-like shape."
Azure Heaven
Bān Gù's *Guest and Host*:
Displaying spiritual virtue,
uniting wind and cloud,
surpassing the vast wilderness,
and striding across the azure heaven.
Shīgǔ said:
Hào hào,
is heaven.
The primordial energy is vast and boundless,
therefore it is called Vast Heaven (Hàotiān);
its color is azure,
therefore it is called Azure Heaven (Cāngtiān).
Bright Heaven
Mǎ Róng's *Ode to Guangcheng*:
Second to the Creator on the Earth,
participating in the divine bestowal in the Bright Heaven.
*Book of the Later Han*
Ninefold Azure
Ruǎn Jí's "Letter to Fuxi" says:
The height of the Ninefold Azure,
swift wings cannot seek its summit:
the depth of the Four Seas,
hidden scales cannot fathom its bottom.
Wáng Jiǎn's "Stele of Qitou Tuo Temple":
Those who look up at the azure color,
cannot know its distance.
The *Zhuāngzǐ* says:
"Is the azure of the sky
its true color?
Or is it that it is so far away, with no limit to where it ends?"
The "Nine Fields" section of
the *Lǚshì Chūnqiū* says:
"The sky has nine fields:
The center is Jūntiān (鈞天),
the east is Cāngtiān (蒼天),
the northeast is Biàntiān (變天),
the north is Xuántiān (玄天),
the northwest is Yōutiān (幽天),
the west is Mǐntiān (旻天),
the southwest is Zhūtiān (朱天),
the south is Yántiān (炎天),
the southeast is Yángtiān (陽天)."
Furthermore, the *Guǎngyǎ* states:
"The nine heavens are:
The east is Hàotiān (皥天),
the south is Chìtiān (赤天),
the west is Chéngtiān (成天),
the rest are the same."
Additionally, the *Tàixuán Jīng* mentions:
"The nine heavens are:
One is Zhōngtiān (中天),
two is Xiàntiān (羨天),
three is Cóngtiān (從天),
Sì gēng tiān,
wǔ zuì tiān,
liù kuò tiān,
qī jiǎn tiān,
bā chén tiān,
jiǔ chéng tiān.
Liù qì
"Zuǒ Zhuàn" says:
"Heaven has six *qì*,
which bring forth the five flavors."
Dù Yù's commentary says:
"The six *qì*
refer to *yīn*, *yáng*, wind, rain, darkness, and light."
Jiǔ guān
"Zhāo Hún" says:
"My lord, do not ascend to heaven!
Tigers and leopards guard the nine gates,
pecking and harming those below."
Wáng Yì says:
"The gates of heaven are nine-layered,
and divine tigers and leopards are made to guard their opening and closing,
pecking and killing those who desire the earth."
Bā zhù
"Tiān Wèn" says:
"What supports the eight pillars,
東南何虧？ What deficiency is there in the southeast?
注曰： The commentary says:
言天有八山為柱， It speaks of Heaven having eight mountains as pillars.
皆何當值？ What do they all correspond to?
東南不足， If the southeast is deficient,
誰虧缺之也。 who has caused its depletion?
《楚辭》 *Chǔ Cí* (Songs of Chu)
九重 *Jiǔ chóng* (Ninefold Heavens)
《天問》云： The "Tiān Wèn" (Heavenly Questions) says:
圜則九重， The heavens are round and ninefold.
孰營度之？ Who planned and measured them?
注曰： The commentary says:
言天圜而九重， It speaks of Heaven being round and ninefold.
誰營度而知之乎？ Who planned and measured and knows about them?
《楚辭》 *Chǔ Cí* (Songs of Chu)
九乾 *Jiǔ qián* (Nine Heavens)
崔駰《達旨》云： Cuī Yīn's *Dá Zhǐ* (Expressing My Intentions) says:
仰探遠乎九乾。 Looking up, I explore the vastness of the Nine Heavens.
注： Note:
九重也。 It is the Ninefold Heavens.
《後漢》 *Hòu Hàn* (Later Han Dynasty)
八維 *Bā wéi* (Eight Cardinal Directions)
東方朔《七諫》云： Dōngfāng Shuò's "Qī Jiàn" (Seven Admonitions) says:
引八維以自道兮， I draw upon the eight cardinal directions to guide myself,
含沆瀣以長生。 and imbibe the mists of heaven to prolong life.
Note:
Heaven has eight directions,
which serve as its framework and order.
*Guanzi* says:
"Heaven is supported by something,
Earth is carried by something.
If it were not supported,
Heaven would have already fallen;
how much more so would man?"
Jiǔ Líng (九靈)
Wáng Bāo's (王褒) "Jiǔ Huái" (九懷) says:
"Ascending the Jiǔ Líng (九靈), I wander in spirit."
Note:
It means to imagine ascending the nine heavens to release one's spirit.
Jiǔ Gāi (九陔).
The "Hàn Shū Yuè Zhì" (漢書樂志) says:
"Concentrating and focusing the mind, soaring through the nine barriers."
Note:
Gāi (陔) means
"layered,"
referring to above the nine heavens.
Sīmǎ Xiàngrú's (司馬相如) "Fēng Shàn Shū" (封禪書) says:
"The Great Hàn's (漢) virtue flows upward through the Jiǔ Gāi (九垓),
and downward traces the Bā Shān (八埏)."
*Guǎng Yǎ* says:
"The boundary of the nine heavens is called Jiǔ Yín (九垠);
beyond the nine heavens, the next level is called Jiǔ Gāi (九陔)."
Commentary says:
Yín 垠
means è 堮, a high bank or edge.
Gāi 陔
means jiē 階, steps or stairs.
It speaks of steps being arranged in a series of nine.
The *Huáinánzǐ*
says, a certain scholar said to Lú Áo 盧敖:
“I have an appointment with Hànmàn 汗漫 above the nine gāi 垓 (the nine layers of heaven)."
Seven Héng 衡 (balances):
The *Xiàojīng Yuán Shénqì* 《孝經援神契》 says:
"The Zhou heavens have seven héng 衡 and six intervals."
Commentary:
"The heavens have seven héng 衡. As for why they are called 'intervals',
from the inner héng 衡 to the middle héng 衡,
and from the middle héng 衡 to the outer héng 衡,
the distance between each totals 117,000 *lǐ* 里.”
Nine Hóng 閎 (gateways):
Yáng Xióng's 揚雄 "Jiě Nán" 《解難》 says:
"Emerald dragons and crimson dragons,
without ascending on floating clouds,
and relying on swift winds,
then they cannot soar through the nine hóng 閎."
Commentary:
"The nine hóng 閎 are
the gates of the nine heavens."
《Hàn Shū》
Ten Principles
Heaven has ten principles:
heaven, earth, *yáng*, *yīn*, water, earth, human, metal, wood, fire,
in total, ten principles.
Heaven also has joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure,
corresponding to those of humans,
to be categorized together;
heaven and humans are one.
《Chūnqiū Fánlù》
Nine Heavens
Wèi Zhāng Yuān's 《Guān Xiàng Fù》 says:
"Ascending the prominent peak to gaze afar,
observing the spiritual images in the nine heavens."
Note:
The nine heavens
are the nine skies.
《Dào Shū》 says:
The nine heavens
refer to Shénxiāo, Qīngxiāo, Bìxiāo, Dānxiāo, Jǐngxiāo, Yùxiāo, Lángxiāo, Zǐxiāo, and Tàixiāo.
《Chǔ Cí》 records:
"From the Red Heaven, he descended to the Great Purity."
Four Boundaries
Beyond the Twenty-Eight Mansions, there are 15,000 *lǐ* each,
which are the extreme ends of the four directions,
This is called the Four Boundaries (sì biǎo).
_Kǎo Língyào_
states: Heaven has Four Boundaries,
to spread its essence and spirit;
Earth has Four Rivers (sì dú),
to produce diagrams and writings.
_Hé Tú_
states: Heaven has Four Boundaries and Three Paths.
The Four Boundaries,
are the Fang Star (fáng xīng);
the Three Paths,
are the three paths between the Fang Star:
the southern space is the Upper Path,
the central one is the Middle Path,
the northern space is the Lower Path.
_Tiānjìng Jīng_
Four Harmonies (sì hé).
_Sānlǐ Yìzōng_ states:
Heaven has Four Harmonies.
The four directions of the Kūnlún Mountains,
where the air is harmonious and warm,
are called Harmonies.
The heavenly path turns to the left,
one degree per day and night.
Turning one degree.
The sun and moon travel leftwards in the sky,
turning one day and night,
Encompassing the four harmonies.
The *Zhou Bi* says:
Heaven and earth have four extremities and four harmonies.
Commentary:
What are referred to as the four harmonies
are called the extremities.
Zi, Wu, Mao, You,
obtain the center of east, west, south, and north.
Three changes.
The "Treatise on Astronomy of the Han Dynasty" says:
The movement of the heavens has a small change every thirty years,
a medium change every hundred years,
a large change every five hundred years,
three large changes make one cycle,
three cycles and it is completely prepared.
Nine positions
Heaven has nine positions,
earth has nine regions,
heaven has three celestial indicators,
earth has three forms.
"Líng Xiǎn"
Eight principles
Heaven has essence,
earth has form;
heaven has eight principles,
earth has five *lǐ*.
Therefore, it can be the parent of all things.
*Sù Wèn* (Simple Questions).
Refining stones to mend the flaws.
*Lièzǐ* says:
Heaven and Earth
are also things.
Things have imperfections,
therefore, in the past, Nǚwā shì refined five-colored stones to mend its flaws,
and severed the feet of the giant turtle to establish the four poles.
*Huáinánzǐ* says:
In ancient times,
the four poles collapsed,
the nine provinces cracked;
the sky did not fully cover,
the earth did not completely support.
Fires blazed without ceasing,
and floods surged without end.
Thereupon, Nǚwā shì refined five-colored stones to mend the azure sky,
severed the feet of the giant turtle to establish the four poles,
killed the black dragon to save Jìzhōu,
and piled up ash from reeds to stop the excessive waters.
Heavenly Pillar.
Gònggōng fought with Zhuānxū to become emperor,
and in anger, he struck Mount Bùzhōu.
He broke the heavenly pillar
and severed the earth's axis.
Gù tiān qīng xīběi,
rì yuè xīngchén jiù yān;
dì bù mǎn dōngnán,
gù bǎi chuān shuǐ lǎo guī yān.
*Lièzǐ*
Táng Lè's "*Dàyán Fù*" says:
"The brave warrior, in his fury, severed the cords of Heaven;
the Big Dipper turned awry, and Mount Tài was leveled."
The celestial palace:
A follower of the Way said that Huángdì rode a dragon and ascended into the clouds,
climbed the morning glow,
and reached the rows of palaces above,
his reversed reflection passing through the celestial palace.
The celestial sphere is like a carriage,
with a canopy from which the sun and moon are suspended;
how can one ascend it?
*Huáng Lǎn Mùjì*
And
Shū Yú of Táng's mother dreamed that Heaven told King Wǔ:
"I order you to give birth to a son,
named Yú,
and I will give him Táng."
When the son was born,
there was a mark on his hand,
saying "Yú,"
so he was named accordingly.
*Shǐ Jì*
Imparting to Chǔ:
Gōngsūn Guīfù arranged for the ruler of Chǔ to meet with him in Sòng.
The people of Sòng sent an urgent appeal to Jìn.
The Marquis of Jìn wanted to come to their rescue.
Bó Zōng said:
"It is not possible.
Heaven is currently bestowing favor upon Chǔ.
We should not contend with them.
Even though Jìn is strong,
can it defy Heaven?"
*Zuǒ Zhuàn*
Looking Up:
Qí Huán Gōng, looking up, said:
"What does a true king value?"
Guǎn Zhòng said:
"He values Heaven."
Huán Gōng looked up.
Guǎn Zhòng said:
"The so-called Heaven
is not the vast, boundless blue sky.
Those who rule over the people
regard the common people as Heaven."
*Shuō Yuàn*
A Dream of Oppression:
Initially,
Mùzǐ left the Shū Sūn clan
and went to Qí.
He married into the Guó clan
and had Mèng Bǐng and Zhòng Rén.
He dreamed that the sky was pressing down on him, and he could not overcome it.
He looked around and saw a man
with a black face and a hunched back,
with deep-set eyes and a monkey-like snout,
shouting to him, "Niu, help me!"
Then he overcame it.
*Zuǒ Zhuàn*
"Heaven's Drunkenness".
The *Xījīng Fù* says:
"In the past, the Heavenly Emperor was pleased with Duke Mù of Qín and granted him an audience,
feasting him with the钧天广乐 (Jūntiān Guǎngyuè) music.
The Emperor was somewhat drunk,
and so made a golden tablet,
granting the use of this land,
and clipping off the Chúnshǒu region."
*Āi Jiāngnán Fù* says:
"To grant Chúnshǒu to Qín,
why was Heaven drunk in this way?"
*Yú Xǐ Zhì Lín* says:
"The proverb says:
'The Heavenly Emperor made Qín tyrannical in his drunkenness,
and gold mistakenly fell as meteorites.'
It is said that Qín Mù Gōng 秦穆公 dreamed of the Heavenly Emperor playing the music of Jūn Tiān 鈞天,
and there was already this saying.
Lǐ Wénráo 李文饒 said:
"In the past, during the Qín 秦 dynasty, the golden tablets were called 'Heavenly Intoxication'."
How could Heaven be constantly intoxicated!
From the *Wén Xuǎn* 文選:
Zhào Jiǎnzǐ 趙簡子 was ill,
and for five days, he did not recognize anyone.
After two days,
he half-awoke and told his officials:
"I was in the Emperor's palace and it was very pleasant.
I traveled with the hundred spirits in Jūn Tiān 鈞天,
where there was magnificent music with nine movements and ten thousand dances,
unlike the music of the Three Dynasties,
and its sound moved people's hearts."
Biǎn Què 扁鵲 told Dǒng Ānyú 董安于:
"In the past, Qín Mù Gōng 秦繆公 experienced something similar,
and after seven days, he awoke
and told Gōngsūn Zhī 公孫支 and Zǐ Yú 子輿:
'I was in the Emperor's palace and it was very pleasant; the reason I stayed so long
was that I happened to be learning.'"
From the *Shǐ Jì* 史記.
"The Man of Qǐ 杞 Worrying about the Sky."
There was a man from the state of Qǐ 杞 who
worried that the heavens and earth would collapse and fall,
leaving him with nowhere to rest his body,
and he stopped sleeping and eating.
Again, there was someone worried about what that other person was worried about,
so he went to explain it to him.
He said:
"The sky is just accumulated *qi* (氣, vital energy).
There is nowhere without *qi*;
it's like stretching, contracting, breathing.
All day long you walk and stop in the sky;
why worry about it collapsing?"
The person said:
"If the sky is really accumulated *qi*,
shouldn't the sun, moon, and stars fall?"
The one explaining it said:
"The sun, moon, and stars are also luminous things within the accumulated *qi*.
Even if they do fall,
they cannot cause any harm."
*Liezi*
"Discussing the Heavens"
The *Comprehensive Meaning of the Five Classics* says:
Zōu Yǎn spoke grandly about heavenly matters,
and was called "Discussing the Heavens."
Liú Xiàng's *Miscellaneous Records* says:
What Zōu Yǎn spoke about was the beginning and end of the Five Virtues,
and the vastness of Heaven and Earth.
His writings discussed heavenly matters,
therefore he was called "Zōu who Discusses the Heavens."
The *Records of the Grand Historian* says:
Yǎn was circuitous, grand, and eloquent,
Therefore, the people of Qí praised him, saying "Tán Tiān Yǎn."
Dreamed of ascending to Heaven.
In Rǔnán, there was formerly the Hóng Xì Pī (鸿郤陂).
During the time of Emperor Chéngdì,
Dí Fāngjìn memorialized to have it destroyed because it was ruined.
Emperor Chéngdì dreamed that he ascended to Heaven,
and the Heavenly Emperor angrily said:
"Why did you destroy my Zhuó Lóng Yuān (濯龍淵)?"
From *The Biography of Xǔ Yáng in the Later Hàn*.
Touching Heaven.
Empress Héxī Dèng once dreamed of touching Heaven.
The celestial sphere was vast and purely blue,
as smooth as maltose candy,
with formations resembling stalactites.
She then looked up, coughed, and drank from it.
She inquired about the dream interpretation,
and they said, "Yáo dreamed of climbing to Heaven,
and Tāng dreamed of reaching Heaven and licking it.
These are all premonitions of sage kings,
and the auspiciousness cannot be expressed."
From the *Book of the Later Hàn*.
Heaven's Head, Heaven's Ears, Heaven's Feet, Heaven's Surname.
The Wú envoy Zhāng Wēn came to visit,
and all the officials went to see him off,
but Qín Mì arrived late.
Wèn (Wēn) asked Mì:
"Does Heaven have a head?"
Mì said:
"It does."
Wēn said:
"In what direction is it?"
He said:
"It is in the West.
The *Book of Poetry* says:
'Then he looked to the West.'
Based on this,
the head is in the West."
Wēn said:
"Does Heaven have ears?"
Mì said:
"Heaven dwells high but its virtue is humble.
The *Book of Poetry* says:
'The crane cries in the marshes,
its voice is heard in Heaven.'
If it had no ears,
how would it hear it?"
Wēn said:
"Does Heaven have feet?"
Mì said:
"It does.
The *Book of Poetry* says:
'Heaven's steps are difficult,
the son does not follow.'
"If it has no feet,
how can it walk?"
Wēn said,
"Does Heaven have a surname?"
Mì said,
"It does."
Wēn said,
"What is the surname?"
Mì said,
"The surname is Liú."
Wēn said,
"How do you know this?"
Mì said,
"The Son of Heaven's surname is Liú,
therefore I know it."
Wēn said,
"Does the sun rise in the east?"
Mì said,
"Although it rises in the east,
it sets in the west."
His answers to questions came forth like an echo to a sound,
thereupon Wēn greatly admired and submitted to him.
*Shǔ Zhì*
Dreaming of a tree breaking through the sky.
Xǔ Zhēnjūn (許真君) and Wú Měng (吳猛) together with Guō Pú (郭璞) met with Wáng Dūn (王敦).
Dūn said,
"Last night I dreamt of using a tree to break through the sky,
"Can abdication achieve perfection?"
Xǔ Jūn said:
"This dream is certainly not auspicious.
"Wood above breaking heaven,
is the character 'wèi' 未 [meaning 'not yet']."
"Your Excellency should not act rashly.
The Jìn 晉 dynasty is certainly not yet in decline."
*Shí'èr Zhēn Jūn Zhuàn* 十二真君傳 (Biographies of the Twelve Perfected Sovereigns)
Zhāng Bīn 張斌 was recommended as a Xiàolián 孝廉 (Filial and Incorrupt),
and dreamed of erecting a pole.
Suǒ Dǎn 索紞 said:
"This is the character 'wèi' 未."
*Qián Liáng Lù* 前涼錄 (Record of the Former Liang)
Tiāngōng 天公 (The Celestial Lord)
In the first year of Jiànwǔ 建武 (era name),
Jupiter trespassed upon Tiānguān 天關 (Celestial Gate).
Yǔ Yì 庾翼 wrote to Yǔ Bīng 庾冰, saying:
"Jupiter trespassing upon Tiānguān 天關,
the divination says, 'gates and bridges will become obstructed'.
Lately, there has been no other trouble in Jiangdong 江東 (the region east of the Yangtze River),
and the river routes are not difficult;
but Shí Hǔ 石虎 has repeatedly closed the gates for years, not allowing communication through envoys.
This is again a sign of Tiāngōng's 天公 (Celestial Lord's) muddled thinking, unable to distinguish black from white."
*Sòng Shū Tiānwén Zhì* 宋書天文志 (Treatise on Astronomy in the Book of Song)
Striking at the Gate
Táo Kǎn 陶侃 dreamed that he grew eight wings,
Flew and ascended to the heavens,
saw the nine layers of the heavenly gate,
and had already ascended eight of them,
but could not enter through one gate,
using his wings to beat at the sky.
The gatekeeper struck him with a staff,
causing him to fall to the ground,
breaking his left wing.
When he awoke,
his left armpit still ached.
Later, he became the commander of eight provinces,
and secretly harbored ambitions of usurpation,
but each time he thought of the omen of the broken wing,
he restrained himself.
*Jìn Shū*
The Heavenly Emperor's face was one foot square.
During the Xiánkāng reign period of the Jìn Dynasty,
there was a scholar named Zhōu Wèi
who died and came back to life.
He said that the Heavenly Emperor summoned him,
and led him to ascend the hall.
He looked up at the Emperor
whose face was one foot square.
He asked those around him,
"Is this the ancient Heavenly Emperor Zhāng?"
They replied,
"The ancient Heavenly Emperor
It has been long since the sage departed;
this refers to the time near Emperor Míng of Cáo."
The Heavenly Gate Opens
"Book of Jin," Biographies:
The ruler of Northern Yan, Féng Bá, once saw the Heavenly Gate open at night,
its divine light blazing,
illuminating the courtyard.
"Book of Northern Qi":
Emperor Wénxuān, Gāo Yáng, when traveling with Emperor Shìzōng past Mount Liáoyáng,
alone saw the Heavenly Gate open,
the others saw nothing.
"Record of Preserved Light":
Yáng Xíjí, when young, saw the heavens open,
within which the clouds and mist swirled turbulently,
with towers and pavilions arranged irregularly,
bright light shone down upon the mountains,
and after a short while, it closed.
"Anecdotes of Wáng Wéngōng":
Dàn, when young, saw the Heavenly Gate open,
within which was his own name.
Liú Xióngfēi, Pacification Commissioner of Sìchuān, also saw the Heavenly Gate open.
Dreaming of the Heavenly Gate Opening
When Xuē Āndū of the Sòng dynasty first campaigned in Guān and Shǎn,
upon arriving at Jiùkǒu,
he dreamed of looking up at the sky,
and saw the Heavenly Gate open,
He said to his attendants,
"Do you see the Heavenly Gate opening?"
When Xiào Wǔ [孝武] attacked the rebellious and ascended the throne,
he sighed and said,
"Is the opening of the Heavenly Gate in my dream an auspicious omen of revival?"
He was enfeoffed as the Baron of Nánxiāng [南鄉] for his merits.
*History of the Southern Dynasties*
Róng Guāng [榮光] During the Yǒngmíng [永明] era,
the sky suddenly had a yellow light shining on the ground,
and no one could understand it.
The Registrar of the Minister of Education presented a *Ode to the Golden Heaven*.
Wáng Chī [王摛] said:
"This is not the Golden Heaven,
it is what is called Róng Guāng [榮光]."
Shìzōng [世宗] was greatly pleased
and appointed him as the Grand Administrator of Yǒngyáng [永陽].
*Book of Qi*
The character "Heaven Center" [天中字] During the Liang dynasty, Shěn Yǔ [沈瑀] was close to Fàn Yún [范雲].
At the end of the Qi dynasty, he once stayed overnight at Yún's [雲] residence.
He dreamt that he was sitting on a beam of the house,
and looking up, he saw the character "Heaven Center" [天中字] that said "Fàn [范] Family Residence".
Yǔ [瑀] told Gāozǔ [高祖] about it.
Gāozǔ [高祖] said:
"If Yún [雲] is able to avoid death,
"This dream can be verified."
*Liáng Yǔ Shū Zhuàn* (梁瑀書傳)
Yún Tíng Gōng (雲亭宮)
profoundly understanding musical scales and measures.
During the Sui dynasty, Wàn Bǎo Cháng (萬寶常) was born intelligent and precocious,
He once encountered ten or so unusual people in the wilderness.
They summoned him to come forward,
and said:
"The Supreme Deity, recognizing your divinely endowed talent for music,
has dispatched officials from the鈞天 (Jūn Tiān) to reveal the essentials of profound mysteries."
They bade him sit,
and instructed him for a long time.
Then, together, they ascended into the sky and departed.
Bǎo Cháng returned home,
having been gone for five days.
Thereafter, he thoroughly investigated all the music of the human world.
None escaped his profound study.
One night,
the immortals he had previously encountered descended upon his home,
saying:
"Do you remember the gathering at Yún Tíng Palace?"
Bǎo Cháng was bewildered for a long time,
but then understood.
One day, he said to his neighbors:
"I was accidentally banished from the immortal palace to the human world,
and I am about to leave.
In ten days, I do not know where I will go."
*Xiān Zhuàn Shíyí* (Gleanings from Biographies of Immortals)
White Jade Tower
Lǐ Hè once, when ill, saw a man in scarlet robes riding a red *qiú*,
with a boy holding a board,
like ancient seal script,
who said,
"The Supreme Deity has newly built a White Jade Tower,
and upon its completion,
summons you to write its record,
for there is exceptional joy in Heaven."
Hè then died.
*Běn Zhuàn* (Original Biography)
After Hè's death,
his mother dreamed that Hè said,
"The Supreme Deity
is a divine and immortal ruler.
Recently, He moved the capital to Moon Garden,
building the White Jade Palace,
and because of my proficiency in composing poetry,
summoned me and several other scholars
to jointly write the record of the new palace.
The Emperor also constructed the Hall of Concentrated Void,
ordering us to compile musical compositions.
Now I am among the divine immortals,
and greatly enjoy myself!
I hope my lady will not worry about me."
*Xuānshì Zhì* (Records from the Xuan Chamber)
*Chén Wài Zhì* (Records Beyond the Dust)
Five Virtues
Emperor Shìzōng of the Zhōu dynasty observed the great flood at Sìzhōu.
He recorded it and asked Dòu Yǎn about it.
Yǎn replied:
"Heaven and earth have five virtues:
moistening, drying, generating, completing, and moving."
*Yù Hǎi Gàn Zhū Yī* (Jade Sea, Deep Pearl, Volume One)
Holding in Hands
Hán Qí governed Qínzhōu.
He was bedridden for several days.
Suddenly, he said:
"I just dreamed of holding the sky in my hands twice."
Later, he assisted Emperor Yīngzōng while he was still a prince.
He aided Emperor Shénzōng while he was in the Eastern Palace.
*Juàn Yóu Lù* (Records of Weary Travels)
Celestial Phenomena Forming Patterns
Páng Jí governed Yán'ān.
On the night of the winter solstice,
in a trance,
he saw celestial phenomena forming patterns,
saying:
"Ten years from now, Páng Jí will become prime minister,
and will assist the Emperor with benevolence."
He gazed at it for a long time before it disappeared.
After ten years, he indeed became chancellor.
*Qū Wěi Jiù Wén*
Jade Capital Golden Gate
Wáng Sù once dreamed of arriving at the golden gate of the Jade Capital.
In the palace hall there was someone in purple robes and a green crown who
said:
"I am the Attendant of the Eastern Gate,
and you, sir, are the Attendant of the Western Gate.
In the past, we used our memorials to censure the world."
After waking from the dream,
he wrote a poem saying:
"It seems I've come from the land of Huá Xū,
in the depths of clouds and mist I saw towers and terraces.
In the moonlight, the chicken window is cold and desolate, hastening [me to wake],
Startled awake from a fleeting life's dream."
In his later years, thinking of the dream of the Jade Capital,
he wrote a poem saying:
"In the blue sky is hidden the White Jade Capital,
my dreaming soul flies into the Phoenix City.
When will I again walk outside the clouds and mists,
Pearly teeth and azure pupils are already permitted to form."
*Gǔ Jīn Shī Huà*
The Library of God
In the early years of Zhènghé,
Fāng, a *cháosǎn* from Pútián, was the magistrate of Wùyuán.
He fell ill with a fever and was confined to bed.
After three days, he awoke and
said:
"I arrived in a city,
where a Daoist priest bowed and said:
'Sir, you are a person from the Táng 唐 dynasty.
In the past, you had secret good deeds, and the Emperor summoned you to the Bái Yù 白玉 (White Jade) Pavilion.
That was where Lǐ Chángjí 李長吉 wrote records.
When you were testing the great Dao of non-action,
and composing, you had an insightful couplet that said:
'The Emperor drilled orifices and lost his soul;
the snake drew feet and lost the cup.'
The Emperor read it and was greatly pleased.
He appointed you as a *xiūwénláng* 脩文郎
with the sole responsibility of writing.
Later, he appointed you as the Yù Huá 玉華 (Jade Flower) Attendant.
Afterward, because you relied on your talent and were envied by many,
you were demoted to the Qún Yù 群玉 (Flock of Jade) Outer Overseer.
The Qún Yù Diàn 群玉殿 (Hall of the Flock of Jade) is the Upper Emperor's library of books.
From then on, meetings with the Emperor became somewhat infrequent.
One day,
the Emperor was touring the Yáo Pǔ 瑤圃 (Jade Orchard) and summoned you.
You were boating on the pond with Sòng Dàohuá 宋道華,
and you had thoughts of a human husband and wife.
You were impeached by an envoy,
banished,
and fell into the human world.
You will return before long.'"
*Yì Jiān Zhì* 《夷堅志》
Chānghé
The "Lí Sāo" says:
"I ordered the gatekeeper of the Emperor to open the gate,
leaning on the Chānghé and gazing for me."
The "Huáinánzǐ" says:
"Pushing open the Chānghé,
submerging the Heavenly Gate."
The commentary says:
"Chānghé
is the gate through which one first ascends to Heaven."
"The Heavenly Gate
is the gate of the Zǐwēi Palace, where the Supreme God resides."
Zhāng Yuān's "Guānxiàng Fù" says:
"The Chānghé solemnly opens wide."
The commentary says:
"The two sections of the palace wall,
opening directly south like a gate, are named the Chānghé Gate."
Zhāng Héng's Fù says:
"I called upon the Emperor's gatekeeper to open the doors,
to meet the Heavenly Emperor in the jade palace."
Tiānmén
The "Hétú Kuòdì Xiàng" says:
"The northwest is the Heavenly Gate,
the southeast is the Earthly Portal."
The commentary says:
"Heaven is deficient in the northwest,
This is Tiānmén (天門, Heavenly Gate);
the earth is not full in the southeast,
this is Dìhù (地戶, Earth Door).
*Hàn Shū Yuèzhì* (漢書樂志, Book of Han, Treatise on Music):
"The Heavenly Gate opens,
vast and boundless."
Commentary:
"The celestial body
is firm and clear."
*Shén Yì Jīng* (神異經, Classic of Divine Wonders): In the great wilderness of the northwest,
there is a golden palace, thousands of *zhàng* high.
Above it is a bright moon pearl,
three *zhàng* in diameter,
its light shining for a thousand *lǐ*.
Within it are golden stairs,
the two palaces are named Tiānmén (天門, Heavenly Gate).
Tiānlù (天路, Heavenly Road)
Méi Chéng (枚乘)'s *Yuèfǔ* (樂府, Music Bureau Poem) says:
"The beautiful woman is in the clouds,
the Heavenly Road is separated without end."
Tiāndǒu (天鬭, Contending with Heaven)
The *Shū* (書, Book of Documents) states:
"The work of Heaven, let the artisans take its place."
The *Zhuàn* (傳, Commentary) says:
"Those who accomplish the work of Heaven and Earth
have never failed to flourish."
From this perspective,
If a ruler of the world [shìzhǔ] desires to enrich those who have contributed nothing,
this is contending with Heaven.
To desire to maintain power for a long time
has never been achieved in that way.
*Qian Fu Lun* (Essays of the Recluse)
*Tiān Jiào* (Heaven's Teachings)
A commoner said:
When previous generations wished to proclaim amnesty,
they always first sent horsemen to travel through the cities and villages,
listening at the street corners.
If all said,
"There will be an amnesty,"
then they knew it was Heaven's teaching.
Truly, if a benevolent ruler [rénjūn] heard this
and thought it was Heaven's teaching and immediately followed it,
there could be no greater mistake.
*Shàng* (Above)
*Tiān Yǔ* (Voice of Heaven)
Tall hats are indistinct,
distantly hearing the voice of Heaven.
*Xú Líng Xiào Yì Sì Bēi* (Xu Ling's Stele for the Temple of Filial Piety)
*Zhāng Gōng* (Drawing a Bow)
The way of Heaven, is it not like drawing a bow?
It presses down the high,
and raises up the low;
it diminishes the excessive,
Supplement what is insufficient.
The Dao of Heaven is:
To diminish what is excessive and supplement what is insufficient.
*Lǎozi*
The circle is not in accordance with the compass.
*Lǎozi* says:
That which is unadorned and reaches the greatest extent has no form,
The Dao which reaches the greatest extent has no measure.
Therefore, the roundness of Heaven is not in accordance with the compass,
And the squareness of the Earth is not in accordance with the set square.
*Wénzi*
Without End
Heaven is round and without end,
Therefore, one cannot observe its form;
Earth is square and without bounds,
Therefore, no one can fathom its gate.
The transformations of Heaven proceed without shape,
The growth of the Earth proceeds without measure.
*Wénzi*
Clear and Bright
The Dao of Heaven is without partiality,
Therefore, it is always correct;
Heaven...
Is always correct,
Therefore, it is clear and bright.
*Shēn Zǐ*
Zhèng's commentary:
*Kǎo Líng Yào* says:
Heaven
is purely *yáng*, clear and bright, and without form.
The sage emulates it
and makes the *xuán jī* and *yù héng* to measure its phenomena.
*Yīn* and *yáng*:
from the zenith southward,
is the *yáng* of Heaven;
from the zenith northward,
is the *yīn* of Heaven.
*Wù Lǐ Lùn*:
Clear *yáng*:
accumulated *yáng* forms Heaven,
therefore Heaven is clear *yáng*.
*Huáng Dì Sù Wèn*:
Begins at *Qiān Niú*.
*Hé Tú Kuò Dì Xiàng* says:
Heaven moves to the left,
originating from *Qiān Niú*;
Earth moves to the right,
originating from *Bì*.
*Shī Zǐ* says:
Heaven expands to the left and begins at *Qiān Niú*,
Earth expands to the right and begins at *Bì* and *Mǎo*.
Deficient in the Northwest
The *Sù Wèn* says:
"Heaven is deficient in the northwest;
therefore, the northwest is *yīn*,
and people's right ear and eye are not as clear as the left.
The earth is incomplete in the southeast;
therefore, the southeast is *yáng*,
and people's left hand and foot are not as strong as the right."
It also says:
"Heaven is deficient in the northwest;
the left is cold, and the right is cool.
The earth is incomplete in the southeast;
the right is hot, and the left is warm."
The commentary states:
"The topography of the Central Plains
is high in the northwest
and low in the southeast.
Now, a hundred rivers converge eastward into the Cang Sea;
thus, the elevation of east, west, north, and south can be known."
The Qi of the Four Directions
The *qì* of the east is thunder,
the *qì* of the south is lightning,
the *qì* of the west is rainbows,
the *qì* of the north is clouds, rain, hail, and sleet,
and the *qì* of the center is dew.
*Zào Huà Quán Yú*
The clerks of Heaven, the envoys of Heaven, the appointed times of Heaven, the taboos of Heaven
— the four seasons
are the clerks of Heaven;
the sun and moon
are the envoys of Heaven;
the stars and constellations
are the appointed times of Heaven;
rainbows, comets, and sweeping stars
are the taboos of Heaven.
. *Huainanzi, Treatise on Astronomy*
Like an Umbrella
The shape of the sky is vaulted like an umbrella,
and it covers the surface of the earth.
It floats above the primal *qi*,
just as if one overturned a cosmetic case to restrain water from flowing away,
because the *qi* fills it completely.
Yú Sǒng, *On Exhaustively Examining Heaven*
A shape like a Cover
It is said:
Zhuānxū made the armillary sphere,
the Yellow Emperor devised the Canopy Heaven theory,
both considering the shape of the sky as a cover.
. *Master Liú's Questions on Calendar Rectification*
A Slanted Cover
The ancients said:
Regarding the forms of Heaven and Earth, there are three:
First is the *Húntiān* (渾天) theory,
second is the *Gàitiān* (蓋天) theory,
and third is the *Xuānyè* (宣夜) theory.
The *Xuānyè* theory
has not been heard of before.
Later, Yú Bǐng (虞昺) wrote the *Qióngtiān Lùn* (穹天論) [Treatise on the Vaulted Heavens],
Yáo Xìn (姚信) wrote the *Xīntiān Lùn* (昕天論) [Treatise on the Dawn Heavens],
Yú Xǐ (虞喜) wrote the *Āntiān Lùn* (安天論) [Treatise on the Settled Heavens],
with various forms and differing appearances,
interspersed among them.
The *Gàitiān* theory also has three variations:
One says that Heaven is like a carriage canopy,
moving within the eight extremes.
Another says that the shape of Heaven is like a bamboo hat,
high in the center and low on all sides;
another says that Heaven is like a tilted carriage canopy,
high in the south and low in the north.
*Tiānwén Lù* (天文錄) [Records of Astronomy]
“Inverted Bowl”
The "Inverted Bowl" theory states that Heaven is flat and upright,
no different from the Earth,
resembling the shape of an inverted bowl.
. *Lùnhéng Shuōyuē* (論衡說曰) [Discourses Weighed and Judged]:
“Chariot Wheel”
The "Chariot Wheel" theory states that Heaven is like a chariot wheel,
ending and beginning again,
jí zé fù fǎn. The extreme reverts.
《Lǚshì Chūnqiū》
《Líng Xiàn》 says:
The sky revolves by means of *yáng*,
The earth remains stationary by means of *yīn*.
Chicken egg
The sky is like a chicken egg,
The earth is like the yolk inside,
Isolated within the sky.
The sky is large and the earth is small.
The sky has water on both its outer and inner surfaces.
Each part of the sky rides on *qì* to stand,
Carrying water and floating.
The sky circles 365 and one-quarter degrees.
Again dividing it in half,
Then half covers the earth above,
And half circles beneath the earth.
Therefore, the Twenty-Eight Mansions are half visible and half hidden.
The sky rotates like the movement of a wheel hub.
《Húntiān Yí》
Ant grinding
The school of *Zhōu Bì* says:
The sky is round like an opened umbrella,
The earth is square like a chessboard.
The sky rotates sideways like pushing a millstone and goes to the left.
The sun and moon go to the right.
天 tiān turns to the left.
Therefore, the sun and moon actually move eastward,
but the sky pulls them westward.
Imagine an ant walking on a millstone.
The millstone rotates to the left while the ant moves to the right.
The millstone spins quickly while the ant is slow.
Therefore, it cannot but follow the millstone in its leftward rotation.
Tiān Jūn (Heavenly Sovereign):
In the towns and states of Mǎ Hán and other countries,
each designates one person to preside over sacrifices.
The name of the heavenly deity is "Tiān Jūn."
(From "Biographies of the Four Foreign Tribes" [in the *Book of the Later Hàn*])
Taking Heaven as elder brother:
The king of the Wa state takes Heaven as his elder brother
and the sun as his younger brother.
At daybreak, he comes out to attend to government affairs,
sitting in the lotus position.
As soon as the sun rises, he ceases handling affairs,
saying:
"I entrust them to my younger brother."
(*Běi Shǐ* [History of the Northern Dynasties])
Names of Heavenly Deities:
The *Wǔ Jīng Tōng Yì* [Comprehensive Meaning of the Five Classics] says:
The greatest of the heavenly deities is called Hàotiān Shàngdì (August Heaven, Supreme Emperor),
which is also Yaòpò Bǎo;
it is also called Tiānhuáng Dàdì (Heavenly Emperor, Great Emperor),
It is also called Tài Yī (太一, the Great One).
Its assistants are called the Five Emperors:
The Azure Emperor of the East, Wēi Líng Yǎng (威靈仰),
The Scarlet Emperor of the South, Chì Biāo Nù (赤熛怒),
The White Emperor of the West, Bái Zhāo Jù (白招拒),
The Black Emperor of the North, Yè Guāng Jì (叶光紀),
The Yellow Emperor of the Center, Hán Shū Niǔ (含樞紐).
Another account says that the Azure Emperor is named Líng Fú (靈符),
The Scarlet Emperor is named Wén Zǔ (文祖),
The White Emperor is named Xiǎn Jì (顯紀),
The Black Emperor is named Xuán Jǔ (玄矩),
The Yellow Emperor is named Shén Dǒu (神斗).
The *Hé Tú* (河圖, Yellow River Map) says:
Its essence in the East is the Azure Dragon,
In the South, it is the Vermilion Bird,
In the Center, it is the Qilin (麟, Chinese Unicorn),
In the West, it is the White Tiger,
In the North, it is
the Xuán Wǔ (玄武, Black Tortoise).
Mù Gōng (木公, Duke of Wood),
is also called Dōng Wáng Fù (東王父, Father King of the East),
is also called Dōng Wáng Gōng (東王公, Duke King of the East),
is also called Yù Huáng Jūn (玉皇君, Jade Emperor Lord),
residing within cloud chambers,
with purple clouds as his canopy,
and blue clouds as his city.
*Xiān Zhuàn Shíyí* (Gleanings from Accounts of Immortals)
Formerly, at the beginning of the Hàn dynasty, there were four or five children
playing a game of drawing on the ground by the road.
One child sang:
"Wearing a blue skirt, entering the heavenly gate,
Saluting the Golden Mother, bowing to the Wooden Duke."
Zhāng Zifáng went forward to greet them, saying:
"These are the jade boys of the Eastern King Duke.
The so-called Golden Mother
is the Western Queen Mother.
The Wooden Duke
is the Eastern King Duke.
Immortals bow to the King Duke, salute the Queen Mother."
*Zhēn Gào* (Declarations of the Perfected)
The *Lǎo Jūn Zhōng Jīng* (Central Scripture of Lord Lao) says:
The Eastern King Father
is the *qīng yáng* (pure *yang*) energy,
the first of all deities.
He governs the East,
residing below on Mount Pénglái.
His surname is Wúwéi,
his given name is Jūnjiě.
The Western Queen Mother
is the *tàiyīn* (great *yin*) energy.
Her surname is Zìrán,
her given name is Jūnsī,
residing below in the golden city of Mount Kūnlún,
with nine layers of clouds of five colors,
At the summit of a ten-thousand-zhang peak.
Directly above are the Běidǒu (Northern Dipper), the Huágài (Canopy) constellation, the Zǐfáng (Purple Chamber), and below, the Běichén (North Star).
It is said that Dōng Wánggōng's name is Ní,
and his style name is Jūnmíng.
Xī Wángmǔ's surname is Yáng, and her given name is Huí.
The Dwarf Zhū Asks Heaven
The dwarf Zhū asked about the height of the sky, saying it was higher than a tall person.
The tall person said:
"I do not know."
Zhū said:
"Although you do not know,
you are still closer to it than I am."
Therefore, for all inquiries,
one must ask those who know.
From *Huáinán Shuō Shān*
The Heavenly Emperor Summons a Singer
Sòng Hè Dàoyǎng was skilled in divination through tortoiseshell cracks.
He encountered a woman who was a professional singer, who fell ill and died.
He divined for her and said:
"This is not death,
but the Heavenly Emperor has summoned her to sing."
He then placed a clod of earth on her heart,
and after a short while, she revived.
*Nán Shǐ Hè*
The Jade Emperor's Abode
Yùdì's residence is always surrounded by red clouds,
and even true immortals are not allowed to see his face.
*Yì Shèng Zhuàn*
Sū Dōngpō's poem says:
"Attendant ministers stand like cranes in the Tōngmíng Hall,
a cluster of red clouds holding up
the Jade Emperor
Jade Capital."
The *Wǔ Xīng Jīng* says:
"In the heavens is the White Jade Capital,
with golden palaces."
The *Língshū Jīn Jǐng Nèi Jīng*:
"The Jade Capital of the upper realm."
A note says:
"The Jade Capital
is the Heaven of Non-Action."
Thirty-six Heavens
From Xuán Dū Jade Capital downwards,
there are a total of thirty-six heavens,
of which twenty-eight are within the Three Realms.
The six heavens of Huánglǔ Heaven, Yùwán Heaven, Hétóng Heaven, Píngyù Heaven, Wénjǔ Heaven, and Seven Luminaries Móyí Heaven constitute the Desire Realm;

the eighteen heavens of Yuèhéng Heaven, Méngyì Heaven, Héyáng Heaven, Gōnghuá Heaven, Zōngpiāo Heaven, Huángjiā Heaven, Tángyào Heaven, Duānjìng Heaven, Gōngqìng Heaven, Jíyáo Heaven, Yuánzǎi Kǒngshēng Heaven, Huángyá Heaven, Jífēng Heaven, Xiàománg Heaven, Wēngchóng Fúróng Heaven, Jiāngyóu Heaven, Ruǎnluò Heaven, Tánshì Heaven constitute the Form Realm;
the four heavens of Xiāodù Heaven, Yuándòng Heaven, Hànpǒng Miàochéng Heaven, and Xiùlè Jìnshàng Heaven constitute the Formless Realm.

Outside the Three Realms are the Four People Heavens, Chángróng Heaven, Yùlóng Téngshèng Heaven, Fàndù Heaven, and Píngyù Jiǎyì Heaven, also known as the Seed People Heavens or the Four Brahma Heavens.
Outside the Four People Heavens are the Three Purity Realms:
Jade Purity, Great Purity, Upper Purity,
It is also named the Three Heavens:
Qīngwēi Tiān, Yǔyú Tiān, and Dàchì Tiān.
The highest is the Dàluó Heaven,
encompassing the thirty-six heavens.
*Língbǎo Běnyuán Jīng Yúnjí Qīqiān*
Dàluó
Dàluó is in Xuándū,
above Yùjīng, the Zǐwēi Golden Tower, with seven-jeweled soaring trees, where qílín and lions are born by transformation,
and the Heavenly Worthies of the Three Epochs govern within it.
The Yuánshǐ Scripture says:
"In the realm of Dàluó, there are no more chaste rulers,
only the aura of the Great Brahman,
encompassing all the heavens.
Above the void, there are natural five-colored clouds,
whose color is dark yellow, called the Yellow Heaven.
Above the Yellow Heaven, its color is blue-grey, called the Azure Heaven.
Above the Azure Heaven, its color is dark and empty, called the Blue Heaven."
Therefore, the hymn says:
"Above the Three Realms,
boundless Dàluó.
Above, there are no forms of the senses,
the cloud layers are lofty."
The Nine Heavens
Of the Nine Heavens, the first heaven is named Yùdān Wúliàng Tiān,
the second heaven is named Shàngshàng Chánshàn Wúliàngshòu Tiān,
the third heaven is named Fànjiān Tiān,
The fourth heaven is named Dōushù Heaven (兜術天),
the fifth heaven is named Bùjiāolè Heaven (不驕樂天),
the sixth heaven is named Huàyìngshēng Heaven (化應聲天),
the seventh heaven is named Fànbǎo Heaven (梵寶天),
the eighth heaven is named Fànmójāyí Heaven (梵摩迦夷天),
the ninth heaven is named Bōlí Dáshù Heaven (波棃荅恕天).
Each of these heavens has three more heavens separately placed within it,
totaling thirty-six heavens.
*Dà Xiāo Láng Zhuàn* (大霄琅傳)
Dàmíng (大冥)
Dàmíng (大冥) is above the nine heavens,
referring to the extreme distance of the dark *qi*,
far beyond the nine *xuán*.
*Dà Dòng Jīng* (大洞經)
Different names
The Xiongnu call heaven Qílián (祁連).
*Hàn Shū* (漢書):
Huò Qùbìng (霍去病) reached Qílián Mountain (祁連山).
Shīgǔ's (師古) commentary quotes *Wèi Shū Zhū Róng Zhuàn* (魏書朱榮傳):
Qílián Pool (祁連池),
the Wei dynasty calls it heaven.
The Western Regions say:
Devadeva (提婆).
*Gāosēng Zhuàn* (高僧傳) 1 translated eight divisions.
The Mongolians say:
Tönggrig (統格落).
*Shū Yuán Jì* (菽園記)
Thirty-three Heavens.
Halfway up Mount Xūmí, at 42,000 *yóuxún*, is the Heaven of the Four Heavenly Kings (*Sì Tiānwáng Tiān*).
The summit of Mount Xūmí is the Heaven of Emperor Śakra (*Dìshì Tiān*).
One level above is the Yāma Heaven (*Yè mó Tiān*).
Above that is the Tuṣita Heaven (*Dōushuài Tuó Tiān*).
The Nirmāṇarati Heaven (*Huàlè Tiān*).
The Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven (*Tāhuà Zìzài Tiān*).
The Heaven of the Multitude of Brahmā (*Fànzhòng Tiān*).
The Heaven of Brahmā's Retinue (*Fànfǔ Tiān*).
The Great Brahmā Heaven (*Dà Fàn Tiān*).
The Heaven of Limited Light (*Shǎo Guāng Tiān*).
The Heaven of Immeasurable Light (*Wúliàng Guāng Tiān*).
The Heaven of Ābhāsvara (*Guāngyīn Tiān*).
The Heaven of Limited Purity (*Shǎo Jìng Tiān*).
The Heaven of Immeasurable Purity (*Wúliàng Jìng Tiān*).
The Heaven of Universal Purity (*Biàn Jìng Tiān*).
The Heaven of Merit-Birth (*Fúshēng Tiān*).
The Heaven of Merit-Reception (*Fúshòu Tiān*).
The Heaven of Broad Arrival (*Guǎnglái Tiān*).
The Heaven of No-Thought (*Wúxiǎng Tiān*).
The Heaven of No-Affliction (*Wúfán Tiān*).
The Heaven of No-Heat (*Wúrè Tiān*).
The Heaven of Good-Seeing (*Shànjiàn Tiān*).
The Heaven of Good Manifestation (*Shànxiàn Tiān*).
The Akaniṣṭha Heaven (*Sè Jìujìng Tiān*).
The Heaven of Boundless Space (*Wúbiān Kōngchù Tiān*).
The Heaven of Boundless Consciousness (*Wúbiān Shíchù Tiān*).
The Heaven of No-Thing-Whatsoever,
the Heaven of Neither-Thinking-Nor-Not-Thinking.
In all, there are twenty-eight heavens.
Below the four heavens,
there are also the heavens of the sun, moon, and stars,
the Cháng Jiāo Heaven,
the Chí Mán Heaven,
the Jiān Shǒu Heaven.
In all, there are thirty-three kinds.
The so-called Thirty-three Heavens
are the palace of the Dìshì Heaven.
The *Yīnběn Jīng*
describes the number of heavens in the Three Realms,
which is the same as that of the Śākya clan, but the names are different.
From *Yǒuyáng Zázǔ*:
Tiān Wēng
Tiān Wēng's surname was Zhāng,
his given name was Jiān,
his style name was Là Kě.
He was a person from Yúyáng.
In his youth, he was unruly,
and had no restraints.
He once set up a net and caught a white sparrow,
which he loved and raised.
He dreamed that the heavenly Liú Wēng rebuked him angrily,
and repeatedly wanted to kill it.
The white sparrow always informed Jiān,
He firmly established defenses in all directions to await them,
but in the end, none could harm him.
The Heavenly Elder (Tiān Wēng) then descended to observe him.
Jiān lavishly prepared a host-guest arrangement.
He then secretly rode the Heavenly Elder's chariot,
mounted a white dragon,
and brandishing a whip, ascended to Heaven.
The Heavenly Elder rode his remaining dragon to pursue him,
but could not catch up.
Once Jiān arrived at the Dark Palace (Xuán Gōng),
he replaced all the officials,
blocked the North Gate,
and appointed the White Sparrow (Bái Què) as Upper Minister Marquis,
decreeing that the descendants of the White Sparrow would not be born in the lower realm.
Old Man Liú (Liú Wēng) lost his governance
and wandered around the Five Peaks, causing disasters.
Jiān worried about this
and appointed Old Man Liú (Liú Wēng) as the Grand Protector of Mount Tài,
in charge of the registers of life and death.
. "Miscellaneous Morsels from Yóu Yáng - Records of Zhū Gāo"
Six-Character Verse on Grotto Heavens
The "Zhen Gao" says:
If people in the world know the names of the six celestial palaces of Fēngdū,
then a hundred ghosts will not dare to harm them.
The six palaces of the grotto heavens are ten thousand *lǐ* in circumference,
and two thousand six hundred *lǐ* in height.
The six palaces of the grotto heavens are the palaces of the six celestial ghost gods.
The first of the six heavens is the Zhòu Jué Yīn Tiān Gōng (紂絕陰天宮),
the second is the Tài Rán Liàng Shì Zōng Tiān Gōng (泰然諒事宗天宮),
the third is the Míng Chén Nài Fàn Wǔ Chéng Tiān Gōng (明辰耐犯武成天宮),
the fourth is the Tián Zhào Zuì Qì Tiān Gōng (恬照罪氣天宮),
the fifth is the Zōng Líng Wáng Fēi Tiān Gōng (宗靈亡非天宮),
and the sixth is the Gǎn Sī Lián Wǎn Lǚ Tiān Gōng (敢司連宛屢天宮).
*Mùfǔ Yànxián Lù* (Unofficial Records of Leisurely Happenings in the General's Office)
*Tiānzhōng Jì*, Scroll 22
Heart
Recognizing the Subtle
The heart
is subtle.
What it recognizes is subtle and minute.
There is nothing that does not penetrate the heart.
*Shìmíng* ("Explanation of Names") says:
"The heart
is the essence of fire.
It is formed from the Five Elements.
Therefore, the human heart is five inches long."
*Yuán Mìng Bāo* ("Profound Destiny Wrappings") says:
"The position of the ruler
is like the position of the heart in the body.
The nine orifices are like the functions of officials.
When the heart occupies its proper place,
the nine orifices follow the correct principles.
The ears and eyes
are the organs of sight and hearing.
When the heart has desires,
objects pass by and the eyes do not see them;
sounds arrive and the ears do not hear them.
Therefore, it is said that when the ruler deviates from the proper way,
those below fail in their duties."
*Guǎn Xīnshù* ("The Art of Governing the Heart") says:
Wisdom dwells
in purifying its palace.
Its gates and palace refer to the mind.
The mind
is the dwelling place of wisdom;
therefore, it is called a palace.
To purify it
is to remove excessive desires.
The supreme
spirit
is the source of wisdom.
When the spirit is clear, then wisdom is bright.
Wisdom
is the storehouse of the mind;
when wisdom is impartial, then the mind is at peace.
*Wén Zǐ*
The mind should be small.
Lǎozǐ said:
In the way of all people,
the mind should be small,
the will should be great,
wisdom should be round,
and conduct should be square.
That which is called a "small mind"
is to consider trouble before it arises,
to guard against calamity and be cautious about the subtle,
(One) dares not indulge their desires;
Those whose aspirations are grand
encompass all nations,
viewing different customs and judgments as equal,
gathering at the center like spokes converging on a hub;
Those whose wisdom is complete
have no beginning or end,
flowing in all directions,
an inexhaustible spring;
Those whose actions are principled
stand upright and unyielding,
pure white and unsoiled,
unchanging in poverty,
and unrestrained in success.
Therefore, the narrow-minded are restricted by the insignificant;
the ambitious embrace everything;
the wise know everything;
the principled have things they will not do.
Sūn Sīmiǎo told Lú Zhàolín,
"One's courage should be great, but one's mind should be cautious;
one's wisdom should be complete, but one's actions should be principled."
The poem says:
"As if approaching a deep abyss,
as if treading on thin ice."
This speaks of being cautious.
"Brave warriors,
bulwarks of dukes and marquises."
This refers to great courage.
"Not swayed by profit,
not troubled by righteousness."
The method of action is,
"Act upon seeing the opportunity,
do not wait until the end of the day."
This is the completeness of wisdom."
*Jiù Táng* (Old Book of Tang)
The Master of Form
The heart is the master
of the form.
The spirit is
the treasure of the heart.
If the form is labored without rest, it will collapse;
if the essence is used without end, it will be exhausted.
Therefore, the sages follow this,
daring not to transgress it.
Using nothing to respond to something,
one must investigate its principle.
Using emptiness to receive fullness,
one must exhaust its joints.
Be tranquil, joyful, empty, and still,
so as to complete one's life.
*Wénzǐ*
The Heart of the State
Lǎozǐ said:
The ruler
is the heart of the state.
If the heart is well-governed, then all the joints are at peace;
if the heart is disturbed, then all the joints are in chaos.
Therefore, those whose persons are well-governed
disregard their limbs;
those whose states are well-governed
forget each other, ruler and minister.
Above,
*Língtái*:
Ten thousand evils must not be allowed into the *língtái*.
Sīmǎ says:
The heart is the platform of the spirits.
“Zhuāng Gēngsāng Chǔ”:
Gōng Chuí used a compass to build,
The compass and square responded to objects without resorting to mental calculations;
therefore, his *língtái* was unified and unfettered.
“Dá Shēng”:
The *língtái* is luxuriant and misty, overlooking the wild fields.
The *língtái* is the heart.
“Huángtíng”:
Heavenly Ruler:
The ears, eyes, nose, and mouth each have their own functions but cannot coordinate with each other.
These are what are called the "heavenly officials."
The heart dwells in the central emptiness and governs the five senses;
this is what is called the "Heavenly Ruler" (*Tiānjūn*).
The sage purifies his Tiānjūn (天君, Heavenly Ruler),
and rectifies his Tiānguān (天官, Heavenly Officials).
*Xúnzi, Tiān Lùn* (荀子, 天論, *Xúnzi, On Heaven*)
The master of spiritual insight:
The heart is the ruler of the body and the master of spiritual insight.
It issues commands without receiving commands;
it restricts itself,
it employs itself,
it deprives itself,
it takes for itself,
it acts by itself,
it desists by itself.
Therefore, the mouth can be coerced to speak (like) Mò (墨);
the body can be coerced to bend,
but the heart cannot be coerced to change its intentions.
*Jiě Bì* (解蔽, Dispelling Obscuration).
The master of the five viscera:
The heart
is the master of the five viscera.
It is that which controls and directs the four limbs,
circulates the blood and breath,
gallops through the realm of right and wrong,
and enters and exits through the gateways of all affairs.
*Huáinánzǐ, Yuán Dào Xià* (淮南子, 原道下, *Huainanzi, Root and Origin of the Way, Part II*)
The essential of all wisdom:
The heart
is the essential of all wisdom;
all things are sought within the heart.
*Yì Lín* (意林, *A Forest of Meanings*)
Difficult to know.
Confucius said:
"The human heart is more treacherous than mountains and rivers,
more difficult than knowing Heaven."
*Zhuāngzǐ*
Spirit and Essence
Zǐ Sī asked Confucius, saying:
"Things have forms and categories,
affairs have truth and falsehood,
one must examine them carefully,
how does one do so?"
Confucius said:
"It is done through the mind.
The spirit and essence of the mind is called sagacity,
to extrapolate numbers and investigate principles,
not allowing doubt to surround (them),
what it observes is difficult even for sages."
*Kǒng Cóng Zǐ* (The Masters of the Kong Family)
Fertilizing the Mind
People all know to fertilize their fields,
but none know to fertilize their minds.
Applying manure to the fields benefits the seedlings and yields grain.
Cultivating the heart is easy to practice and achieves what is desired.
What is meant by cultivating the heart?
Extensive learning and wide knowledge.
What is meant by easy to practice?
The single desire to stop lewdness.
*Mencius, Seen in Imperial Readings*.
Like a mirror.
The mind of a perfect man is like a mirror; it neither goes to meet things nor anticipates them.
It responds to things but does not retain them.
Therefore, it can overcome things without being harmed.
*Zhuāngzǐ*.
Righteous control.
The eyes love colors,
the ears love sounds,
the mouth loves flavors.
They receive these things and are pleased by them,
but they do not know what is beneficial or harmful;
these are desires.
Eating them does not bring peace to the body,
hearing them does not conform to the Way,
seeing them is not beneficial to one's nature.
The three palaces (senses) vie with each other.
That which uses righteousness as control
is the heart.
*Huái Quán Yán*.

"Tiānzhōng Jì" (Records from the Center of Heaven), Volume 36
Classics
*Jīng* (Classic)
*Jīng*, means path. A classic is also a model. Like a path, it leads everywhere, and it can be used constantly.
*Shì Míng* (Explaining Names)

Writings created by sages are called *jīng* (classics), while writings composed by the virtuous are called *zhuàn* (commentaries). Explaining meaning by referring to existing texts is called *gǔ* (exegesis), and explanations based on chapters and
sentences are called *zhù* (annotations).
*Bówù Zhì Shūchāo* (Excerpts from the Record of Extensive Things)
The writings composed by virtuous people are called *jì* (records), *zhāngjù* (chapters and sentences), *jiě* (interpretations), *lùn* (discussions), and *dú* (readings).
*Yùlǎn* (Imperial Readings)
The five classics establish the laws, which govern the universe, are verified by diagrams and images, are validated by the Three Kings, and are applied to the Four Seas.
*Chūnqiū Yǎn Kǒng Tú* (The Spring and Autumn Annals Expanded by Confucius)
The Three Extremes' unchanging instructions are written in the classics. Classics are the eternal and ultimate *dào* (way) and the unchangeable grand teachings.

The *Yìjīng* (Book of Changes) spreads through the Ten Wings, the *Shūjīng* (Book of Documents) marks the Seven Visions, the *Shījīng* (Book of Poetry) lists the Four Beginnings, the *Lǐjīng* (Book of Rites) rectifies the Five Constant Virtues,

the *Chūnqiū* (Spring and Autumn Annals) has five categories, and its meaning reaches the extreme of human nature and emotion, and its language is crafted with literary principles. It can be said to be like rain falling across Mount Tài and a river irrigating a thousand *lǐ*.
Praise says: "Molding the spirit of nature, the treasure house of literature. Deep and vast,
the ancestor of all words."
*Wénxīn Diāolóng* (The Literary Mind and the Carving of Dragons)
The orthodox classics are the source of the art of the *dào*, and the writings of the philosophers are streams that deepen them. They are like
auspicious stars assisting the three luminaries and thick forests supporting tall mountains.
*Bàopǔzi* (Master Who Embraces Simplicity)

Nothing exceeds

Establishing ruler and subject, setting up honor and lowliness, blocking what is gradually developing, preventing what has not yet emerged—nothing exceeds the *Lǐ* (禮, Rites); lamenting the way of kings,

grieving over the politics of the time—nothing exceeds the *Shī* (詩, Poetry); guiding Yin and Yang, showing misfortune and regret—nothing exceeds the *Yì* (易, Changes); making clear good and evil, knowing

decline and flourishing, uttering pronouncements—nothing exceeds the *Chūnqiū* (春秋, Spring and Autumn Annals); measuring distance, describing the nine provinces—nothing exceeds the *Shàngshū* (尚書, Book of Documents);

Nothing surpasses *Music* for understanding human emotions and influencing customs; nothing surpasses *Shang Han* (the works of Shang Yang and Han Fei) for governing criminal law and scrutinizing legal techniques;
nothing surpasses *History* for recording dynasties and documenting governance and chaos. Followers of Han Shi Ke and the like mixed and confused them,
and the world saw that their talents were easy to acquire and their ideas easy to accept, so every family wrote a book, and every person wrote a legal method. Refined
gentlemen cast aside their pens and inkstones and looked down upon them.

Confucius said, "The *Yì* (易) is *yì* (易), change, and unchangeable. It governs the three virtues, and is the container and key to the Dao
. The *Yì* (易) is its virtue, bright and open in all directions, simple to establish principles. Heaven is brilliantly clear, with the
sun, moon, and stars arranged in order, penetratingly subtle without a door, concealing the divine without a hole, without trouble or disturbance, tranquil and
unwavering; this is its *yì* (易). Change is its breath. If heaven and earth did not change, they could not communicate their breath. The five elements
alternate to their end, and the four seasons replace each other; rulers and ministers take their images, and changing principles are moved; what can be dispersed will cease, and what is obsessed will
fail; this is its change. The unchangeable is its position: heaven is above, earth is below, the ruler faces south,

Huái'ān
When the Jìn 公子 Gōngzǐ Chóng'ěr was in trouble,
he fled to Qí.
Duke Huán of Qí married him to a woman
and gave him twenty chariots.
The 公子 Gōngzǐ settled down,
but his followers thought this was unacceptable.
They planned to leave under a mulberry tree. A silkworm girl was on top of it.
She told Jiāng Shì.
Jiāng Shì killed her and said to the 公子 Gōngzǐ,
"You have ambitions for the four directions.
I have killed anyone who heard of it."
The 公子 Gōngzǐ said,
"There was nothing of the sort."
Jiāng said,
"Going about being comfortable and settled will truly ruin your reputation, 公子 Gōngzǐ, it must not be."
Jiāng plotted with Zǐ Fàn,
got him drunk, and sent him off.
When he sobered up, he chased Zǐ Fàn with a spear.
Zuǒ Xī 23
Weaving Shoes
King Zhuāng of Chǔ sent
someone with one hundred *jīn* of gold to hire Mister Běi Guō.
The mister said,
"Your subject has a wife who wields the broom and dustpan,
I wish to consult with her."
He then said to his wife:
"Chǔ desires to make me their minister.
If I become minister today, I will have harnessed teams and lined-up riders,
and eat a square zhang of food before me.
What do you think?"
The woman said:
"You, sir, make a living by weaving shoes,
eating thin porridge and wearing rabbit-skin slippers,
and have no worries about being startled or anxious. Why?
Because you do not interfere with things.
Now, if you were to have harnessed teams and lined-up riders,
the space you occupy would be no more than the size of your knees;
if you were to eat a square zhang of food before you,
the sweetness you taste would be no more than a single piece of meat.
Is it worth sacrificing the peace of the size of your knees
and the taste of a single piece of meat for the worries of the state of Chǔ?
How could that be?"
Thereupon, he did not accept the appointment,
and left with his wife.
From *Hán Shī Wài Zhuàn*.
Throwing down his dustpan,
Lǎo Lái Zi fled the world
and farmed on the south side of Mount Méng.
The King of Chǔ arrived at his gate in a carriage,
and said:
"The orphan heir to the state
wishes to see you, sir."
Lǎo Lái said,
"Yes."
His wife said,
"I have heard that
those who can be fed with wine and meat
can be followed with whips and cudgels;
those who can be granted official salaries
can be followed with axes.
Now, sir, you eat their wine and meat,
and receive their official salary;
you will be controlled by them.
Can you avoid disaster?
I cannot bear to be controlled by others."
She threw down her basket and hoe and left.
Lǎo Láizi told Zǐ Huán, "I will worry for you again."
Then he left without looking back
and stopped in Jiāngnán.
"Biographies of Exemplary Women"
Weeping over Riches
Táo Dāzi governed Táo for three years,
but his reputation did not rise.
His family became three times richer.
His wife alone held their child and wept.
His mother-in-law angrily said:
"How unlucky is this!"
The woman said:
"My husband's ability is meager yet his official position is high,
this is called inviting disaster;
without merit yet the family prospers,
this is called accumulating calamity.
I have heard that on Nánshān (南山) there is a black leopard,
even with mist and rain for seven days it does not descend,
what does it eat?
It desires to moisten its fur and create beautiful patterns,
therefore it hides itself and avoids harm,
dogs and pigs do not choose their food in order to fatten themselves,
sitting and awaiting death only.
Now, my husband does not cultivate virtue yet his family grows ever richer,
signs of ruin and destruction are already visible."
A year later, Dá Zǐ (答子) was indeed executed for robbery.
